primary_result: R10 passes the preregistered category-C privileged fixed-region feasibility audit on the exact 384-image Haze4K development population. A shared D_ref/D_rep 8x8 action map chosen from no-op, positive-full and negative-full reaches a worse-operator mean gain of 0.2389403581 dB (grouped-bootstrap LCB95 0.2199980764), exceeds the best dual-operator-safe whole-image action by 0.0877762751 dB (LCB95 0.0767817028), and exceeds a pixel-area- and action-histogram-preserving spatial shuffle by 0.1815458683 dB (LCB95 0.1663672348). Both folds meet the frozen materiality lines, region-minus-global CVaR5 is noninferior, and the selected regional oracle has zero severe and hard image events. This establishes material spatial and signed-action heterogeneity as a privileged development ceiling under the frozen action bank; it does not establish that observable inputs can recover the action map or that the policy is deployable.
gate_reasons: All 384 clean-image groups and 768 paired operator units were evaluated. R5 targets replayed exactly with zero mismatches and maximum absolute difference 0; no-op renders had zero mismatches; the maximum tile-partition SSE discrepancy was 1.1368683772161603e-13.
The primary worse-operator region gain is 0.2389403580740129 dB with LCB95 0.21999807644614275 dB, above the frozen +0.020 dB materiality line.

Region-minus-safe-global gain is 0.08777627513253528 dB with LCB95 0.07678170280953148 dB, and region-minus-spatial-shuffle gain is 0.18154586833943226 dB with LCB95 0.1663672347924294 dB; both exceed the frozen +0.005 dB increment line.
Region-minus-global CVaR5 is 0.003733224278027169 dB with LCB95 0.0014543381992183386 dB, above the frozen -0.005 dB safety margin; region severe and hard counts are both zero.

Fold 0 and fold 1 independently meet all three point materiality lines: region gains are 0.24978769447812885 and 0.22809302166989695 dB, region-minus-global gains are 0.08282726024615683 and 0.09272529001891378 dB, and region-minus-shuffle gains are 0.1834712879261728 and 0.17962044875269176 dB.

Mixed no-op/active support occurs in 348/384 images (0.90625; exact-binomial LCB95 0.8725749078419742), and bidirectional positive/negative support occurs in 294/384 images (0.765625; LCB95 0.7199948254450557). Mean pixel areas are 0.415283203125 no-op, 0.3684488932291667 positive and 0.21626790364583334 negative.

Every active tile met the +0.005 dB local gain requirement under both operators, with zero local safety or materiality violations. All 16 name-seeded shuffles had zero action-histogram and zero action-pixel-area violations. Region gains are highly consistent across D_ref/D_rep (Pearson 0.9998417049132378).

All protected-data permissions remained false. No training, model inference, candidate generation, checkpoint loading, confirmation, canary or locked-test access occurred; R5 and R9 terminal decisions remain unchanged.
competing_explanation: The strongest competitor was that the useful headroom is already captured by one dual-operator-safe whole-image action, or that apparent regional benefit reflects only the action histogram or numerical oracle noise. It is not supported under the frozen development contract: the regional ceiling exceeds the safe whole-image ceiling by 0.0877762751 dB with LCB95 0.0767817028, and it exceeds spatial shuffles that preserve both action-tile counts and action-pixel areas by 0.1815458683 dB with LCB95 0.1663672348. The material positive and negative pixel areas and the 294/384 bidirectional-image count further rule out a one-tile directional artifact. A remaining competitor is observability: target-selected regional utilities may be real but not recoverable from deployable image features. R10 does not test that competitor and therefore authorizes only a new observability-contract review.
limitations: R10 is a category-C post-hoc privileged development feasibility audit on the same 384 Haze4K development images used by R5-R9. It is not independent confirmation or external validation and cannot change the R5-R9 terminal decisions.

The regional action map uses clean-target outcomes and requires each active tile to achieve at least +0.005 dB under both frozen operators. It is a nondeployable oracle; its zero severe/hard count is conditional on this privileged construction and does not demonstrate learned-policy safety.

The conclusion is specific to the frozen 8x8 partition, three-action bank, historical renderer and D_ref/D_rep operators. It does not justify grid, action-magnitude, threshold, smoothing, subgroup or architecture search on the reused development population.

R10 has no light-haze, heavy-haze, protected-region or semantic labels and does not establish that the selected actions align with those human-interpretable regions. Native-shape summaries are descriptive, not subgroup confirmation.

No per-seed stability question exists because R10 performs no fitting or stochastic model inference; the fixed bootstrap and shuffle seeds only make the audit deterministic. Model-training seed stability remains untested.

PASS authorizes only review and preregistration of one independent region-observability contract. It does not authorize training, inference, policy execution, threshold tuning, confirmation, canary, locked-test access, deployment or external-validation claims.
